newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rouble lower on client, non-resident selling.
newsitem.headline: Rouble lower on client, non-resident selling.

text.p: The rouble eased on an inflow of funds from the Treasury bill market, bank client selling and wider central bank rates, dealers said on Friday.
roubles/dollar Dec 27 midday Dec 27 early Dec 26 close
United Investment Bank chief dealer Alexander Suchkov said rouble supply was sufficient as non-residents were selling roubles they were receiving from maturing T-bills.
He added approval by the lower chamber of parliament of a 0.5 percent tax on purchases of foreign cash had had no affect so far as the law must still be passed by the upper house and President.
Dealers said the tax, although applied only to cash purchases, could eventually affect the interbank market by pushing up commission rates.
"The central bank has made its rates wider and it made dollar buying more interesting. Bank clients are seeking dollars as well," Inkombank dealer Dzhamil Asfari said.

He added some banks could reduce their T-bill investments after the central bank said it would cut the average yield on government Treasury Bills and OFZ bonds for non-residents to 12.5 percent from 13.0 percent beginning January 16.
